$schema_note: Conformance vectors for ChannelFilter. A store may translate the filter into a query instead of returning every row, which is an optimization and is the store's to verify: the library's re-check drops rows the filter excludes but cannot recover a row that was never returned, so an under-selecting pushdown is undetectable at runtime. Each case lists records, a filter, and the ids that must survive, in that order. `role` names are the Rust variant names the wire uses: SenderKind for helpers, ReplicaRole for replicas. Ids are decimal strings because the same table is driven from TypeScript, where `JSON.parse` cannot hold a u64. `library/tests/channel_filter_conformance.rs` drives this against `ChannelFilter::matches`, which is the same predicate the library re-checks with; every SDK's suite drives it against its own helper.

cases.name: a default filter selects everything
cases.why: Every field's empty value means 'do not restrict'. A pushdown that treats an empty `ids` as `IN ()` returns nothing and silently stops the protocol acting on any channel.

cases.name: empty ids does not restrict
cases.why: The commonest pushdown bug: `WHERE id IN ()` is not the same as no clause.

cases.name: a null role does not restrict
cases.why: `role` is an optional, not a list. Absent means any role, which is distinct from an empty list meaning the same thing for the other fields.

cases.name: role restricts to exactly that role
exclude is applied after ids and overrides it
cases.why: An id named by both `ids` and `exclude` is excluded. A pushdown that ORs the two, or applies exclude first, returns it.

cases.name: exclude applies with no ids restriction
exclude overrides a full ids list
an id not present selects nothing rather than erroring
ids above 2^53 are matched exactly
cases.why: Ids cross the SDK bridges as decimal strings because `JSON.parse` rounds anything larger. A binding that parses them as numbers matches the wrong channel.

cases.name: excluding a large id does not exclude its rounded neighbour
cases.why: 18446744073709551615 and 18446744073709551614 collapse to the same f64. Excluding one must not drop the other.

cases.name: a default filter selects every member
role narrows to the source
cases.why: How the protocol finds the single member holding Source before a succession.

cases.name: exclude-self with a role restriction
cases.why: The shape the removal path uses: every member that is not this device and not leaving. Order of the survivors decides the successor, so returning too few changes who inherits.

cases.name: excluding the only match selects nothing
